# Results — Study 782 (CEO-Name-Length)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
number of letters in a company's CEO surname predicts its stock's return**. Shape B: a
dollar-neutral **long longest-surname / short shortest-surname** tercile book, rebalanced
monthly, over a fixed 40-name large-cap universe. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `a7f273eb002d` (40 names + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 40 large caps + `SPY`, one combined panel: 2,889 rows, 2015-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Characteristic | **hardcoded**: `len(CEO surname)` for each name, a **STATIC 2026-06 snapshot** — CEO turnover through history is deliberately NOT tracked (disclosed; defensible only because the label is inert by design). Range 2 (AMD/Su) … 11 (MCD/Kempczinski), mean 6.05, sd 1.80 |
| Cross-section | 137 balanced month-ends × 40 names, 2015-02-28 → 2026-06-30 |
| Sort / book | terciles: short = 13 shortest surnames, long = 13 longest; dollar-neutral, equal-weighted within legs, monthly rebalance. Positive LS ⇒ "longer surnames earn more" |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the monthly LS return; Wilson hit-rate interval; 20-seed × 200-draw **label-shuffle placebo**; leave-one-ticker-out jackknife; alternate quantile cuts; costed net leg |
| Neutrality | book is dollar-neutral but not beta-neutral: realised LS beta to SPY ≈ **−0.31** |

## The long/short book — long longest-surname tercile, short shortest (dollar-neutral)

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| monthly LS mean | **−0.930%** |
| monthly LS sd | 3.559% |
| *t* (n = 137) | **−3.058** |
| annualised Sharpe | −0.905 |
| hit rate (positive months) | 58/137 = 42.3% (Wilson [34.4%, 50.7%]) |
| annualised LS mean | ≈ **−11.2%/yr** |
| short-leg (shortest surnames) mean monthly return | +2.326% |
| long-leg (longest surnames) mean monthly return | +1.396% |

The nominal spread is negative and "significant" (*t* = −3.06): the **shortest-surname**
tercile out-earned the longest by ~0.9%/month. **But this is a confound, not a signal**
(see below).

## Why the number is spurious — read this before you get excited

The shortest-surname tercile *is* the mega-cap-tech winners list:

- **short leg (bought by shorts):** AAPL (Cook), AMZN (Jassy), NVDA (Huang), TSLA (Musk),
  AMD (Su), ORCL (Catz), QCOM (Amon), TXN (Ilan) … — the 2015–2026 tech melt-up.
- **long leg:** IBM (Krishna), CSCO (Robbins), MCD (Kempczinski), PEP (Laguarta), WMT
  (McMillon), BAC (Moynihan), GS (Solomon), CMCSA (Roberts) … — the laggards/value side.

So the "surname-length factor" is really **short-tech / long-value in disguise**, arrived at
by a coincidental alignment between short surnames and the megacap-tech cohort. Three fatal
problems:

1. **Static-snapshot look-ahead.** The 2026 CEO surname is stamped onto the *entire*
   2015→2026 history, so the label implicitly "knows" which names became winners.
2. **No mechanism.** There is no channel by which orthography of a surname moves a stock.
3. **Overstated evidence.** The one-sample *t* treats 137 months as independent, but the
   book is a **fixed** portfolio — one persistent ~11-year sector bet (Sharpe −0.9),
   concentrated in 2020 (−36%/yr) and 2026 (−34%/yr). The effective sample size is a handful
   of sector-years, not 137 months.

## Label-shuffle placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws)

| observed LS mean | placebo mean (sd) | two-tail p | draws |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.930% | −0.214% (0.407%) | **0.0385** | 4,000 |

The permutation p is only **borderline** (≈ 0.04), and it is obtained *after* choosing the
direction and the best-looking spec — exactly the multiple-testing setting where a ~0.04 is
not evidence of anything real.

## Jackknife (leave-one-ticker-out) — LS *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−3.058**; across all 40 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−3.447, −2.232]**. "Jackknife-stable," yes — but stability of a confound is still a
confound: dropping any single name can't undo a whole-cohort sector tilt.

## Robustness — alternate quantile cuts

| cut | mean/mo | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| quintile (q = 0.20) | −0.986% | −2.17 |
| tercile (q = 0.33) | −0.930% | −3.06 |
| median-split (q = 0.50) | −0.695% | −3.48 |

The sign is consistent across cuts — because the underlying sector tilt is present at every
breakpoint, not because surname length means anything.

## Tradability — net of costs (monthly rebalance, conservative full-turnover charge)

| leg cost | mean/mo | *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | −0.930% | −3.06 | −0.90 |
| net @ 5 bps | −1.030% | −3.39 | −1.00 |
| net @ 10 bps | −1.130% | −3.72 | −1.10 |

Costs make the *short* look "stronger" (you're shorting a negative window), but you would
simply be shorting the megacap-tech cohort against value for a decade — an ex-post sector
bet, not a repeatable name-length edge, and one with no forward basis.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.23 (sd 1.22); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  the sort does not manufacture a spread on an inert label.
- **Planted slope +0.004 (seed 798):** LS mean +0.876%/mo, *t* = **+4.27**.
- **Planted slope +0.008 (seed 798):** LS mean +1.779%/mo, *t* = **+8.66** — a *real*
  characteristic→return slope is recovered monotonically. The machinery works; the real
  tape's spread is a confound, not a planted slope.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The nominal stats cross the bar (*t* = −3.06, placebo two-tail p ≈ 0.04, jackknife-stable [−3.45, −2.23], consistent across cuts) — so it is **not** indistinguishable from noise. But it is a textbook **confound**: a static end-of-sample CEO snapshot turns the sort into a fixed short-tech/long-value sector bet (short leg = AAPL/AMZN/NVDA/TSLA/AMD), the monthly *t* overstates evidence for a fixed one-decade portfolio (real edge is one ~11-yr sector bet, Sharpe −0.9, driven by 2020 & 2026), and there is zero mechanism. Real number, wrong cause — hence Weak, not Real, and not None. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The "edge" is an unrepeatable, look-ahead-contaminated sector coincidence dressed up as a name-length factor; it has no forward basis and would just be a levered ex-post bet against megacap tech. |

**In one sentence:** sorting stocks by how long the CEO's surname is produces a
significant-looking −0.9%/month long/short — but only because short surnames happened to
belong to the megacap-tech winners (Cook, Jassy, Huang, Musk, Su), so the "signal" is a
static-snapshot sector tilt with no mechanism: Weak, and a Mirage to trade.
